summary: Catalyst Retail — Multipath reassembly producing duplicate/truncated completions during peak traffic; escalation and post-incident action plan
description: Issue summary: During two afternoon traffic peaks on 2026-03-10 Catalyst Retail experienced repeated fragmented and duplicate completions for conversational endpoints. Impact: user-facing duplicates and truncated completions causing business-critical checkout dialogs to fail and a ~30% increase in tokens billed during incident window. Root symptom: multipath reassembly module failed to deduplicate partial fragments when a subset of multiplexed responses were routed across failover paths.
impact: - Customer-facing duplicate completions and truncated replies for session-based chat flows. - Elevated token consumption leading to billing spike and customer complaint. - Customer reported lost conversions during peak.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send 4 concurrent streaming chat requests tied to same session affinity token to model rw-instruct-large-8b-quant in us-east during sustained 200 RPS
2) Induce a transient 10-20% packet loss in the router (simulated via iptables) while triggering autoscale events
3) Observe reassembly logic in gateway producing duplicated chunks and out-of-order final completions
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z router WARN multiplexed-recovery: reassembly timeout for session=cr-session-77
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z serving-runtime ERROR kv-cache: pending-eviction race detected shard=3
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z api-gateway INFO stream: partial-chunk-forwarded path=/v1/chat/stream request_id=req-9f7a
investigation_notes: Initial triage by SRE (E. Chen): correlation between routing failovers and duplicate fragments; packet loss amplification seen when autoscaler brought up new endpoints.
Observed that reassembly sequence numbers were occasionally replayed when one path responded slower and the other replayed cached prefix.
Hypothesis: concurrent failover + aggressive prefix caching + reassembly logic did not dedupe identical fragment ids across transport paths.
Telemetry: increased retransmit counts (x5) and 429s absent; no CPU/GPU OOM observed.
mitigation: Applied immediate temporary throttle on concurrent session affinity (config updated in router to cap session fanout to 2)
Disabled cross-path prefix caching for sessions flagged with high fanout
Rolled a hotfix to reassembly module to add fragment-id deduplication and extend reassembly timeout by 250ms (deploy PR #4578) in us-east then eu-west
resolution: Hotfix merged and rolled to prod (serving-runtime v2026.03.10-hotfix1) across affected regions
Router config change made persistent via runbook and reverted throttle after validation
Billing credit issued to customer for the window (see comments for amount) and formal apology sent
Monitoring alert created to track fragment duplicate rate and token delta
postincident_actions: 1) Schedule deep-dive with reassembly and routing teams on 2026-03-18
2) Add e2e chaos test for cross-path packet loss in CI (ticket INT-91234)
3) Update runbook: on detection of duplicate fragment rate>0.5% auto-apply session fanout cap
4) Audit billing aggregation to detect token deltas and auto-calc credits
customer_communications: 2026-03-10 16:20 UTC: initial acknowledgment to Catalyst Retail support contact (Z. Martinez) confirming we are investigating
2026-03-10 19:05 UTC: detailed incident update explaining failover-induced fragment duplication and next steps
2026-03-11 09:10 UTC: notification of hotfix deployment and planned credit
credit_resolved: USD 12,500 credited to Catalyst Retail invoice for incident window (approved by Finance on 2026-03-11)

E. Chen (SRE): 'Hotfix adds fragment-id dedupe and we observed duplicate rate drop to <0.01% in canary.'
